title: Approval before acting
product: Microsoft Entra ID and Exchange Online
use_case: Hold the Microsoft 365 account takeover cleanup and phishing purge actions until someone approves them in Teams or Slack, then run them once, record the approver on the case, and do nothing on a denied or expired request.
trigger: Platform Events, source Case, event Comment Added, with the Only When filter in SETUP.md, so it runs only on the chat bridge's approval decisions.
connections: Taegis.MicrosoftGraphAPI 2.12.2, the Microsoft Graph API connector Sophos manages, to run the held actions
Taegis.Case 1.0.5, the case connector Sophos manages, to read the request and comment the outcome
The library's chat bridge, required: it carries the approval from Teams or Slack to the case
requires: The library's chat bridge, Microsoft 365 account takeover cleanup 1.2.0 or Phishing triage and purge 1.1.0 with Ask for approval first on, Teams case chat sync 1.3.0 or Slack case chat sync 1.1.0 to post requests, and Sophos Fusion playbooks under Security Operations > Automations
mdr_note: Sophos MDR doesn't run or watch this playbook. It runs only what a request on the case lists, and the requesting playbooks act only on self-managed cases unless you turn on Include Sophos-managed cases there.
rollback: Enable the account if it was disabled, turn the inbox rules back on, dismiss the user's risk in Entra ID, and restore moved email from Recoverable Items. A password reset and revoked sessions can't be undone. To stop approvals, turn this playbook off: requests then stay unanswered and expire.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: This playbook runs the Microsoft 365 actions that account takeover cleanup and phishing triage and purge hold for approval, once someone approves the request in Teams or Slack through the library's chat bridge. It trusts only decisions the bridge's API credential wrote and requests a playbook wrote, runs each request once, and does nothing on a denied or expired request.
notes:
Setup:
- It needs the chat bridge, with the bridge's API credential client ID as Chat bridge author ID, and Teams case chat sync 1.3.0 or Slack case chat sync 1.1.0 to post requests.
- Turn on Ask for approval first, with dry run off, in account takeover cleanup 1.2.0 or phishing triage and purge 1.1.0. A request needs a case.

How it works:
- It reads the decision from the case, not from the event, and trusts it only when Sophos Fusion recorded the bridge's credential as its author and nobody edited it.
- It trusts a request only when it has the same author as this playbook's own comments, the identity every playbook's case comments get, and nobody edited it.
- Before acting it comments that it has the decision, waits five seconds and reads the case again; the earliest decision on a request wins. Expiry is checked against when the bridge wrote the decision.
- Isolate host isn't in it: no library playbook isolates yet, and it would make every user add a Sophos Endpoint connection.

Testing:
- On 2026-11-16 the dsl passed playbookValidateDSLV2 with no errors or warnings in us01 and eu02, and a renamed copy imported, exported (same apart from whitespace and connector order) and deleted in eu02.
- In us01, renamed copies ran against a test Microsoft 365 tenant and a test case, with signed requests shaped like a Teams outgoing webhook's sent to the live chat bridge.
- Approved, a takeover request disabled the account, reset the password, revoked sessions, turned off two inbox rules and confirmed compromise, read back in Entra ID, the mailbox and the audit log; the reset's request wasn't in the execution log. A phishing request moved the email to Recoverable Items, read back in the mailbox.
- Dry run changed nothing. A denied request, an approval after a deny and an approval a minute after a one-hour request expired ran nothing, and the user read back unchanged.
- The same decision typed in the console, or written by another API credential, ran nothing and wrote nothing. A request written by another credential was refused.
- Two decisions written in the same second ran the request once; the bridge refused a second approval. No execution log held a password, token or webhook URL.

Known gaps:
- No human has approved from a real Teams channel or Slack workspace yet; Slack Approve and Deny ran only in the repo's tests.
- Requests came from made-up detections and a hand run, not a real ITDR finding or Microsoft detection.
